newsitem.title: USA: RJR sees $600 mln first payment under accord.
newsitem.headline: RJR sees $600 mln first payment under accord.

text.p: RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp said Tuesday that it expects its initial payment under a recently reached tobacco accord would be $600 million.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, RJR said it believes implementation of the tobacco agreement would "increase the costs and reduce the consumption of (R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co's) tobacco products in the United States.
The company warned that this "could have a significant negative effect on the business of (R.J. Reynolds) and the stated financial position" of RJR Nabisco Inc and the tobacco unit.
The agreement, reached last Friday, would require cigarette companies to pay $368.5 billion over 25 years to compensate states and smokers and to fund programs to help people quit smoking.
Of that total, Tobacco companies would be required to make an initial $10 billion payment under the agreement and multi-billion annual payments thereafter.
The deal also sets goals of reducing teen smoking by 42 percent in 5 years, 58 percent in 7 years and 67 percent in 10 years or cigarette companies would be penalized by as much as $2 billion a year.

Despite the uncertainties the tobacco giant says it may face if the tobacco accord is finalized, RJR said the proposals contemplated by the agreement "offer a measure of relief from certain litigation that could otherwise materially affect the results of operations or cash flows."
